A1.justification: Both PDFs describe APB by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial rewriting and reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original MuJoCo adaptation experiments, behavior-cloning results, and random-backbone evaluations in Figures 4–7 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 reports original MuJoCo adaptation, extended-horizon evaluation, behavior cloning, linear-probing comparisons, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The shared backbone, task-specific linear adapters, and frozen-backbone adaptation remain; random backbones already appeared in v1. However, Section 5.1 changes APB's underlying optimization from TD3 to SAC losses, and Algorithm 1 replaces trajectory-block adaptation with transition-by-transition replay updates. These revise optimization within the retained architecture.

E1.justification: V2 removes the reported Hopper-rand and Walker-rand dynamics-shift evaluations from Table 1 and the result figures, retaining four reward-based scenarios. It adds extended-horizon RL evaluation in Figure 6, beyond the long-horizon BC evaluation already present in v1. This substantially changes the tested distribution shifts.

E2.justification: V2 adds a post-backbone-only linear-probing comparator in Figure 8 and a frozen random-backbone comparator to BC in Figure 7. Its random-backbone RL study compares against standard RL, whereas v1 Figure 7 compared random and meta-trained backbones. The six main meta-RL comparators—MAML, ANIL, CAVIA, PEARL, VariBAD, and Meta-DT—remain.

E3.justification: The reported APB optimizer and update schedule change from TD3 with trajectory-based update blocks to SAC with per-transition updates. V2 introduces RL evaluation with evaluation horizons exceeding training horizons, probing-only controls, and computational-cost evaluation. The random-backbone Cheetah-vel plot also extends from 50,000 steps in v1 Figure 7 to 100,000 in v2 Figure 4.

E4.justification: V2 adds an explicit test of adapting both linear layers versus only the output layer, a random-backbone BC control, extended-horizon RL robustness tests, and parameter/computational-efficiency analysis. It reworks the existing random-backbone analysis and removes the dynamics-shift tests. These materially change the evidence about which components and conditions explain APB's effectiveness.

E5.justification: Both versions report RL curves averaged over 10 seeds with one-standard-deviation bands and BC means with 95% confidence intervals across 10 seeds. The added RL comparisons follow the existing reporting practice; no new significance-testing or repeated-run procedure is specified.

E6.justification: Several APB curves change in the corresponding Figure 5: for example, Cheetah-vel to Cheetah-dir ends near 600 in v1 and 1,200 in v2 at 200,000 steps. The changed optimization prevents interpreting this as a same-setting gain. V2 also adds probing, extended-horizon, random-backbone BC, and cost results, while removing Hopper/Walker entries. Table 3 newly reports 6,906 versus 219,606 trainable parameters for Cheetah.

T1.justification: V1 Section 4.2's adaptation-error definition, support-coverage analysis, Lipschitz bound in Theorem 2, and its Appendix A.1.4 proof are removed. The policy-matrix decomposition and permutation-based policy-structure theorem remain, with the decomposition moved to Appendix A.1 and revised exposition. The removal substantially reduces the formal theory beyond renumbering or relocation.

C1.justification: V1 presents APB primarily as a sample-efficient meta-transfer RL method. V2 replaces that headline with competitive performance and improved generalization through structural constraints, promoting the existing random-backbone observation to a central contribution. Extended-horizon generalization becomes prominent, while the claim of adaptation where representative meta-RL baselines struggle is retained.

C2.justification: V2 emphasizes architectural inductive bias and explains the RL–BC difference through interactive data collection versus fixed, limited demonstrations. The earlier training-support coverage interpretation disappears. Discussion adds explicit limitations concerning extension of the theory to deep RL and the unresolved contributions of architecture versus meta-parameter quality, while removing the earlier capacity–coverage discussion and diffusion/transformer proposal.

D1.justification: V2 removes v1's parameter-noise levels, initialization scales, reset schedules, trajectory counts, update counts, and detailed exploration-selection and matched-budget descriptions from Table 2 and the implementation appendix. It adds explicit SAC identification and parameter counts, FLOP estimates, and iteration times with an estimation rule. These are substantial documentation changes; omitted descriptions alone do not establish that the corresponding mechanisms were disabled.

R1.justification: Within the retained PEFT/transfer/meta-RL positioning, v2 adds classical multitask and inductive-bias references, strengthens distinctions based on matrix-level theory, and adds SAC and cost-estimation citations. It prunes parts of the broader survey and exploration literature. Publication updates for existing works, including D'Eramo and Raghu, do not constitute new cited research.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statement, experimental narrative, and discussion are extensively rewritten around structural constraints and generalization. Contributions become a structured list, Section 4.2 changes focus, and the appendix is reorganized from A.1–A.7 into A–H. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the scientific additions.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout. Retained illustrations are resized and relocated; experimental grids change from six tasks to four; BC panels gain a third bar; and new probing plots and a computational-cost table appear. Tables and algorithm placement are also substantially reorganized.

improvement.justification: The new probing and random-backbone BC controls strengthen the architectural argument, and v2 tempers the earlier sample-efficiency claim. However, experimental coverage narrows, substantial implementation documentation disappears, and the new central horizon and timing evaluations lack numerical horizon settings and hardware information. These gains and reproducibility limitations leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
